## Statement

Most of the quantities this entry calls computable but not computed are computed and published. Connectivity and minimal path length between treatments are in Thom et al. (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329); contrast-specific evidence paths and per-study contribution are in Papakonstantinou et al. (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3) and shipped as netmeta::netcontrib; component estimability has a signal-flow graph in Li, Shih and Tu (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), written in answer to the same complaint this entry makes; and precision-based ranking of the next study design is in Nikolakopoulou et al. (doi:10.1002/sim.6608). The development package cpaic, which lives on GitHub and cannot be installed from CRAN, already computes connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, per-contrast estimability and contrast-specific edge influence. What is genuinely open is that these diagnostics are not routinely reported in NMA outputs, that articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration and removal vulnerability are still missing, and that there is no value-of-information machinery for deciding which study's individual data to acquire.

## Why it is open

The quantities exist in papers and in scattered implementations but not in standard NMA output, so an analysis can rest entirely on one articulation edge or one study without that dependence appearing anywhere a reviewer would see it. Component networks are worse, because information flows through the component design matrix rather than through visible treatment edges; note also that null-space dimension is a linear-algebra property of that matrix rather than a graph algorithm, and nullity alone does not settle whether a requested contrast is estimable. Acquisition decisions remain informal because expected information gain and the value of individual-data placement cannot come from topology alone: they require a target contrast and population, a sampling model, priors and a decision utility, and no such machinery has been built for evidence networks. Design also cannot substitute for data, since where no evidence exists for the required contrast an optimal design still requires someone to collect it.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Thom, White, Welton & Lu, Automated methods to test connectedness and quantify indirectness of evidence in network meta-analysis, Res Synth Methods 2019;10:113-124](https://doi.org/10.1002/jrsm.1329) | Graph algorithms for connectivity, indirect connection and minimal path length between treatments, covering the articulation and minimal-bridge questions, with R and Stata code. |
| [Papakonstantinou et al., Estimating the contribution of studies in network meta-analysis: paths, flows and streams, F1000Res 2018;7:610](https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.14770.3) | Contrast-specific paths of evidence and per-study contribution, that is, vulnerability to removal of a study; implemented as netmeta::netcontrib. |
| [Li, Shih & Tu, Graphical evaluation of evidence structure within a component network meta-analysis, Res Synth Methods 2023;14:596-607](https://doi.org/10.1002/jrsm.1623) | Signal-flow graph over components showing which component effects are identifiable and which need more evidence, written in response to the same complaint this entry makes about component networks. |
| [Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis & Salanti, Planning future studies based on the precision of network meta-analysis results, Stat Med 2016;35:219](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.6608) | Ranks candidate future study designs and sample sizes from network structure and precision, covering the design-prioritization half of this entry. |
| [netmeta::netcontrib reference manual](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/netmeta/html/netcontrib.html) | Shipped implementation of the contribution matrix in network meta-analysis, evidence that per-study contribution is available to practitioners today. |
| [Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio & Welton, Value of Information for Clinical Trial Design: The Importance of Considering All Relevant Comparators, PharmacoEconomics 2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0) | Value-of-information trial design that accounts for the full comparator set, the natural starting point for ranking candidate bridging studies by expected decision value. |
| [cpaic connectivity, estimability and edge-influence diagnostics (development package, GitHub commit 9d150e9)](choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca) | Unreleased development package, not installable from CRAN. Implements treatment-network connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, per-contrast row-space estimability, and a contrast-specific edge-influence diagnostic that reports whether individual data inform the contrast at all. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Make the existing diagnostics routine rather than rebuilding them: bring connectivity, contribution, component estimability and design-precision tools into standard reporting for treatment and component networks, and add what is genuinely missing, articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration and removal vulnerability. Build expected-value-of-information methods on top by specifying the target contrast, population, sampling model, priors and decision utility, so candidate new edges, individual-data acquisitions and bridging studies can be scored by their effect on identification and on the decision. Existing value-of-information work for multi-comparator trial design (doi:10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0) is the natural starting point.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Connectivity, evidence-flow contribution, component estimability graphs and precision-based design of the next trial are all published and partly implemented in netmeta; what is missing is that they are not routinely reported in NMA outputs, and there is no value-of-information machinery for deciding which study's IPD to acquire.

**The source titled this.** "Graph and value-of-information diagnostics for network design" The title names graph diagnostics as an open item, but the audit found connectivity, evidence-flow and component-estimability methods published and partly shipped in netmeta.

**The source said.** "The report lists computable structural quantities that evidence and component networks should report (articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, null-space dimension, contrast-specific paths of component information, vulnerability to removal of a study or component, centrality of IPD placement, expected information gain from adding an edge) and proposes Bayesian experimental design and active learning to rank which IPD to acquire or which bridging trial to run."

**What was wrong with it.** The source listed articulation treatments, minimal bridge sets, null-space dimension, contrast-specific information paths and vulnerability to study removal as computable but not computed. The literature auditor found four published methods covering most of them, one of which ships in netmeta, and GPT-5.6 Sol found rank, null space, bridging components, per-contrast estimability and edge influence already implemented in the unreleased cpaic development package; what survives is routine reporting and value of information for individual-data acquisition.

**Dissent.** grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Pieces of the agenda already exist; the integrated reporting-and-design stack does not. Value-of-information methods for multi-comparator / network-aware research prioritization and trial design are active (e.g. Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio, Welton, PharmacoEconomics 2024 on VOI when all relevant comparators matter; longer Welton/Ades-style EVSI tradition). That partially substantiates ranking candidate bridging trials or evidence acquisitions by expected information for decision. Graph algorithms can in principle compute articulation points, bridges, and related connectivity; NMA practice already has leave-one-out / influence style checks and geometry plots (netmeta and CINeMA ecosystem). What remains open is the report’s full computable suite as standard output: articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, component-design-matrix null-space dimension, contrast-specific component information paths, IPD-placement centrality, and design scores tied to those quantities. I found no 2024–2026 package release or merged PR that implements that diagnostic battery for treatment and component networks as routine reporting. Design still cannot invent missing likelihood for a contrast.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **partially-solved / overstated.** Most of the listed 'computable but not computed' quantities are computed, published and shipped. Connectivity, indirect connection and the minimum number of steps between a treatment pair: Thom, White, Welton & Lu, Res Synth Methods 2019;10:113-124 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329), with R code and a Stata implementation. Contrast-specific paths of information and vulnerability to removing a study: Papakonstantinou et al., F1000Res 2018;7:610 (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3), the proportion contribution matrix, shipped as netmeta::netcontrib. Component estimability specifically: Li, Shih & Tu, Res Synth Methods 2023;14:596-607 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), a signal-flow graph over components, motivated by the exact complaint in this entry's why_open. Freeman et al. (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023;23:208) add CNMA-UpSet, heat map and circle plots. Design-side: Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis & Salanti (Stat Med 2016;35:219, doi:10.1002/sim.6608) compute which study design and sample size to run next from NMA precision, extended in Trials 2019 (doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2). Genuinely open: null-space dimension reporting, centrality of IPD placement, and formal VOI for IPD acquisition.

    Cites doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3: Contrast-specific paths of evidence and per-study contribution, i.e. vulnerability to removal of a study; implemented as netmeta::netcontrib..
    Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623: Directly answers the component-network complaint: a signal-flow graph over components that shows which component effects are identifiable and which need more evidence..
    Cites doi:10.1002/sim.6608: Ranks candidate future study designs and sample sizes from network structure and precision, i.e. the design-prioritization half of this entry..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **partially-solved / overstated.** C1 is straightforward for articulation treatments, but an articulation component needs an explicit bipartite or hypergraph definition and is not equivalent to statistical estimability. C2 and structural leave-one-out versions of C6 are computable once the bridge set is defined. C3 is a design-matrix linear-algebra calculation, not a graph algorithm, and nullity alone does not determine a requested contrast. C4 requires a model and weighting rule and can be non-unique in cyclic or rank-deficient networks. C5 and C7 cannot be obtained from topology alone: expected information gain and the inferential value of IPD require a target contrast and population, sampling model, sample size, overlap, priors, and usually a decision utility. C8 through C10 are sound with those ingredients, and C11 reports the source label. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, cpaic_connectivity already returns connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, rank, null space, and per-contrast estimability, while edge_influence reports contrast-specific edge weights and whether IPD placement informs the contrast. Thus the blanket claim that the quantities are not computed is false, although articulation or cut-set enumeration, removal vulnerability, and model-based value-of-information design remain open. Very high is justified for estimability and fragility diagnostics, not for the entire active-learning bundle.
    Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements treatment-network connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, and per-contrast row-space estimability..
    Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements a contrast-specific estimating-weight diagnostic and identifies whether an IPD edge contributes to the requested contrast..

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **partially-solved / supported-with-caveat.** Pieces of the agenda already exist; the integrated reporting-and-design stack does not. Value-of-information methods for multi-comparator / network-aware research prioritization and trial design are active (e.g. Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio, Welton, PharmacoEconomics 2024 on VOI when all relevant comparators matter; longer Welton/Ades-style EVSI tradition). That partially substantiates ranking candidate bridging trials or evidence acquisitions by expected information for decision. Graph algorithms can in principle compute articulation points, bridges, and related connectivity; NMA practice already has leave-one-out / influence style checks and geometry plots (netmeta and CINeMA ecosystem). What remains open is the report’s full computable suite as standard output: articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, component-design-matrix null-space dimension, contrast-specific component information paths, IPD-placement centrality, and design scores tied to those quantities. I found no 2024–2026 package release or merged PR that implements that diagnostic battery for treatment and component networks as routine reporting. Design still cannot invent missing likelihood for a contrast.
    Cites 10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0: Shows VOI-based trial design should account for the full comparator set (network-relevant), supporting information-gain ranking of new evidence relative to multi-arm decision problems..
    Cites 10.1002/sim.10072: Not a graph-diagnostic resolver; listed only if needed for multi-source computation. Prefer omit if empty required—use only VOI paper as primary..
